NPTEL Online Certification Course
             Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee
Course Name: Introduction to Application of Artificial Intelligence to Robotics
                             Instructor: Prof. Pushparaj Mani Pathak

                 WEEK 12: ASSIGNMENT 12

   Q.1  Why is face cropping performed before DeepFace processing?

         (A) To convert speech into text

          (B) To isolate the facial region that is relevant for emotion analysis

          (C) To convert RGB information into depth information

         (D) To publish the image directly to the ROS2 topic

          Explanation: Face detection identifies the region of interest, after which the cropped
            facial image is processed for emotion estimation.

          Refer slide10 of lecture 56: Demonstration of AI in Humanoid Robot


   Q.2   Suppose facial emotion estimation requires 80 ms while speech processing requires
         120 ms. If the two pipelines operate independently and concurrently, ignoring fusion
           delay, what is the approximate time (in ms) until both are available?

         (A) 40

          (B) 80

          (C) 120

         (D) 200

          Explanation:  With  concurrent  processing,  the  combined  availability  time  is
          determined by the slower pipeline: max(80,120) = 120 ms.


   Q.3   Which combination describes the sensing principle of the Intel RealSense D415?

         (A) Monocular RGB imaging only

          (B) Stereo vision with active infrared projection

          (C) LiDAR with ultrasonic ranging

         (D) Thermal imaging with passive infrared sensing

          Explanation: The D415 combines RGB imaging with stereo vision and active IR
           projection for 3D information.

          Refer slide15 of lecture 57: Demonstration on KUKA KR5 Industrial Robot

slides.title: Q.4  A KUKA KR 5 robot performs the following repeated motion:
slides.text:
Q.4  A KUKA KR 5 robot performs the following repeated motion:

           •  Moves 300 mm horizontally and 200 mm vertically from its initial position
             along a single straight-line path.

           •   Returns to its initial position along the same straight-line path.

           •  Repeats the complete cycle 12 times.

     Assume the robot operates at 60% of  its maximum speed of 8.2 m/s, ignoring
       acceleration and deceleration time. Determine the total distance travelled and the ideal
        total motion time.

      (A) 8.65 m and 1.76 s

      (B) 8.31 m and 1.69 s

      (C) 16.62 m and 3.38 s

      (D) 9.60 m and 1.95 s

       Explanation:

      The one-way distance is 𝑑= √(0.300)2 + (0.200)2 = 0.3606 m

      The robot returns along the same path, so the distance per cycle is:

                                  𝑑cycle = 2(0.3606) = 0.7212 m
      For 12cycles:

                                     𝑑total = 12(0.7212) = 8.65 m
      The operating speed is:

                  𝑣= 0.60(8.2) = 4.92 m/s
       Therefore:

                                       8.65
                       𝑡=   = 1.76 s
                                       4.92


Q.5  A student claims: “AMCL and SLAM perform exactly the same localization task
      because both estimate robot position”. What is the best correction?

      (A) AMCL builds the occupancy map, whereas SLAM only generates velocity
      commands.

      (B) SLAM simultaneously builds a map and estimates position, whereas AMCL
       estimates pose using an existing occupancy map.

      (C) SLAM is exclusively a visualization tool, whereas AMCL is a simulator.

      (D) AMCL performs global planning, whereas SLAM performs local planning.

Explanation: The key distinction is that SLAM couples mapping with localization,
      whereas AMCL performs pose estimation using LiDAR, an occupancy map, and
      odometry.

      Refer slides12, 22 of lecture 58: Demonstration in ROS


Q.6   Which combination most directly explains why ROS2 is suitable for autonomous
       navigation?

      (A) Modular architecture + sensor integration + real-time navigation

      (B) Building Editor + Model Editor + GUI plugins

      (C) Occupancy map + PGM format + XML

      (D) Gazebo rendering + RViz visualization + URDF

       Explanation: These are explicitly listed as reasons for using ROS2 for autonomous
       navigation.

      Refer slide4 of lecture 58: Demonstration in ROS


Q.7  Why  is combining LiDAR and RGB-D information useful for local cost map
       generation?

      (A)  Both sensors measure exactly the same quantity and therefore eliminate
      computation

      (B) LiDAR provides wide angular coverage while RGB-D provides depth and can
       detect low/off-plane obstacles

      (C) RGB-D replaces LiDAR for 360° scanning

      (D) LiDAR provides semantic object classes while RGB-D only measures wheel
       velocity

       Explanation: The lecture specifically contrasts LiDAR's 360° field of view and long
      range with the RGB-D camera's depth information and ability to detect low/off-plane
       obstacles.

      Refer slide8 of lecture 59: Mobile Robot Demonstration


Q.8   For a differential-drive robot with wheel radius 𝑟= 0.1 m and wheel separation 𝐿=
       0.5 m. If the wheel angular velocities are 𝜔𝑅= +5 rad/s and 𝜔𝐿= −5 rad/s, which
       pair correctly describes the robot's motion?

      (A) 𝑣= 0.5 m/s, 𝜔= 0 rad/s - straight motion

      (B) 𝑣= 0 m/s, 𝜔= 2 rad/s - in-place rotation

      (C) 𝑣= 0 m/s, 𝜔= 0 rad/s - stationary

Q.9  A robot nearly collides with a worker, but no injury occurs. The engineering team
       decides not to record the event because "nothing happened." Which principle is
       violated?

      (A) Near-misses should be logged and reviewed

      (B) Data should always be deleted

      (C) Simulation should replace testing

      (D) Learned components should control safety-critical paths

       Explanation: The safety standards explicitly recommends logging and reviewing every
       near-miss or unexpected behaviour, even when no harm occurs.

      Refer slides20, 21 of lecture 60: Application Domains, Ethics, Safety, Future of AI
       Robotics, Course Review & Career Pathways


Q.10 A cobot operates near humans. Which feature provides physical impact-energy
       absorption, independent of software safety limits?

      (A) Redundant sensing

      (B) Mechanical compliance

      (C) Safety-rated zones

      (D) Emergency-stop logic

       Explanation: Soft joints and back-drivable actuators provide mechanical compliance
        that absorbs impact energy.

      Refer slide16 of lecture 60: Application Domains, Ethics, Safety, Future of AI
       Robotics, Course Review & Career Pathways
